name: Sylvan Learning
line: Sylvan tests, then teaches a plan in tutoring sessions. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review happen at every problem.
description: AMP vs Sylvan Learning: Sylvan tests, then teaches a plan in sessions. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review are continuous, at every problem.
verdict: Sylvan Learning starts a child with the Insight Assessment, then teaches a personal plan in sessions with a live teacher, at a center or online [12][1]. In AMP, assessment and teaching are continuous. Every answer updates the learner's level and sets the next problem, and each problem carries its own hint, lesson and worked answer.

reasons.title: Continuous assessment
reasons.body: AMP has no separate test. Every answer, right or wrong, updates the learner's level in that part of math and sets the next problem: new work within reach, a gap to close, or an old skill due back. Sylvan starts with the Insight Assessment, a computer-adaptive test given before the plan is made, one subject per assessment [12][1]. Sylvan says it shows how a child performs compared with other students in the same grade [11].

reasons.title: The problem is the unit
reasons.body: In AMP, everything a learner needs hangs off the problem in front of them: a hint that gives the first step, a lesson with a worked example, a video lesson, the worked answer afterward, and links to the skills it builds on and leads to. In Sylvan the unit is the session. A Sylvan-certified teacher works with students at a low student-to-teacher ratio, in sessions that typically run about an hour, scheduled with the center, at a center or online [5][1]. Across 55 studies, worked examples improve performance in math [9].

reasons.title: Continuous review
reasons.body: In AMP, learned skills come back in ordinary practice, at growing intervals, mixed with other math. Sylvan's comparison sheet says its approach focuses on what a child needs without repeating skills already learned [12]. In a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders, mixed and spaced practice scored 62% a month later, against 38% for practice in blocks, on a test the researchers wrote [8].

reasons.title: Moving on, and going back
reasons.body: In AMP a learner shows a skill by getting it right without help, more than once, and moves on. An answer given after a hint or a lesson is marked as helped and does not count. Repeated misses send practice back to what the skill builds on. At Sylvan, tutors adapt to the child's skill level and pace, and SylvanSync, its instructional system, tracks progress [12]. Its guarantee, for SylvanSync Math and Reading in grades 3 to 12, is stated as skills mastered in hours of instruction [10]. We found no rule in the pages we read for what counts as mastering a skill.

rows.range: Kindergarten through grade 12, from homework help to pre-calculus [1].
rows.start: A separate computer-adaptive test, the Insight Assessment, given before the plan is made, one subject per assessment [12][1].
rows.teaching: A live Sylvan-certified teacher at a low student-to-teacher ratio, in sessions of about an hour, at a center or online [5][1].
rows.next: A personal plan from the assessment. SylvanSync places the child and tracks progress, and tutors adapt to skill level and pace [1][12].
rows.mastery: The guarantee counts skills mastered in hours of instruction, grades 3 to 12 [10]. We found no rule in the pages we read for what counts as mastered.
rows.review: Its comparison sheet says it focuses on what the child needs without repeating skills already learned [12].
rows.adult: A Sylvan teacher teaches. The family requests the assessment and schedules sessions, most often 2 to 4 hours a week [1][5].
rows.reports: A parent portal with online progress tracking, and regularly scheduled progress meetings [12].
rows.evidence: A growth claim that names no study [4]. Evidence for ESSA lists SylvanSync Mathematics with no rating [6].

theirs: Sylvan Learning is a tutoring brand with locally owned centers and live online sessions [2][3]. It teaches math from kindergarten through grade 12, from homework help to pre-calculus, including algebra, fractions, geometry, trigonometry, and probability and statistics [1].

A child starts with the Insight Assessment, a computer-adaptive test, and the center builds a personal plan from it [12][1]. A Sylvan-certified teacher works with the child at a low student-to-teacher ratio, in sessions that typically run about an hour, at a center or live online with the same plan [5][1]. SylvanSync, Sylvan's instructional system, places the child and tracks progress, and a reward system gives prizes and tokens for effort and perseverance [12].
credit: A live teacher works with the child at a low student-to-teacher ratio, in person or online [1][5].
Tutors adapt to the child's skill level and pace [12].
Help with school homework, from kindergarten through pre-calculus [1].

theirs: Sylvan's about page says that, based on independent research, its students see "up to two to three times more academic growth" than other students [4]. The page names no study, sample or design.

We found no outcome study of Sylvan's math tutoring on its site and no What Works Clearinghouse intervention report for it. Evidence for ESSA lists SylvanSync Mathematics, the name Sylvan gives its math program, with no rating and the note "No studies met inclusion requirements" [6][10].

Tutoring as a whole has been studied widely. Across 263 randomized trials the pooled effect was 0.40 standard deviations, and 0.16 to 0.22 for large U.S. programs measured on standardized tests [7]. Those are averages across many tutoring programs, not results for Sylvan.
ours: The two findings that bear on this comparison: worked examples improve math performance across 55 studies [9], and practice that mixes and spaces topics scored 62% against 38% for practice in blocks a month later, in a randomized trial that meets What Works Clearinghouse standards without reservations [8]. AMP applies both at every problem.

AMP's own outcome studies are planned: growth on a national test against hours of use, then comparison groups, then randomized trials. Each will be registered before it starts and published whatever it finds. The research behind each part of AMP is in our report, and AMP is open source.

them: Your child learns best with a teacher working beside them, in a room or on camera.
amp: You want assessment, teaching and review in the same practice, with no separate tests.
You want a hint, a lesson and the worked answer at every problem.
You want learned skills to keep coming back in practice.
Your learner is at different levels in different parts of math.
Your child goes to Sylvan and you want checked practice between sessions.

questions.question: How is AMP different from Sylvan Learning?
questions.answer: Sylvan starts with an assessment, then teaches a personal plan in sessions with a live teacher [12][1]. AMP has no separate test: every answer sets the next problem, each problem carries its own teaching, and learned skills return in ordinary practice.

questions.question: Does Sylvan Learning work?
questions.answer: Sylvan's about page cites independent research for up to two to three times more growth, but names no study [4]. Evidence for ESSA lists SylvanSync Mathematics with no rating, because no studies met its inclusion requirements [6].

questions.question: Can a learner use both?
questions.answer: Yes. They are separate programs. AMP places a learner from their first answers, whatever else they use.
